domain_label: VoIP Deployment, Number Porting & Call Quality
purpose: How a business VoIP reseller takes a signed phone-system deal from discovery to stabilized live service: mapping seats and features to how the business actually answers calls, choosing between new phones, softphones and reused devices, porting the customer's numbers without ever putting them at risk, proving the site network can carry voice with QoS and failover, configuring and verifying E911 dispatchable locations as a hard gate, and executing a trained, tested, reversible cutover that hands a documented system to recurring support.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

deployments serve US small-business customers (dental offices, trucking dispatch, restaurants, motels, small offices) of a business VoIP reseller; regulatory obligations are named as classes and must be verified current for the jurisdiction at deployment time

the reseller may operate under an agent, reseller-of-record, or white-label model; the deployment mechanics here apply across models while the economics of those models live in the channel-economics KB
the customer's established business number is treated as the single most valuable asset touched by the project, and porting sequences are designed so it is never exposed to loss
carrier and platform procedures differ in detail; nodes describe carrier-agnostic mechanisms plus the per-carrier verification step, never one vendor's exact screens or timelines as universal fact
exclusions: channel model selection and economics - agent vs reseller vs white-label, who owns the customer, the bill and the risk, niche selection, offer packaging and competitive positioning belong to the channel-economics-and-segments KB

running the recurring service book - support model and carrier escalation, churn signals and prevention, seat and feature expansion, contract/SLA hygiene, renewals and account-review cross-sell belong to the recurring-service-and-expansion KB

invented commission rates, per-seat prices, port fees, bandwidth figures or savings percentages stated as fact; monetary and performance quantities appear only as mechanisms (how the number arises, what moves it, how to verify it on this deal) or as qualitative bands

asserting current E911, USF-class contribution, telecom-tax or call-recording-consent requirements as settled legal advice; this KB names the obligation class and requires verification of current rules in the customer's jurisdiction by a qualified professional or the platform's compliance resources
guaranteed-uptime or guaranteed-savings claims of any kind without a verified basis (tested failover behavior, the platform's own published commitments, or the customer's actual bills)
designing or migrating alarm-monitoring, elevator-phone or other life-safety communication paths; these are surveyed, flagged and referred to the licensed responsible vendor, never self-performed
personalized legal, tax, financial or medical-privacy advice for the customer's business

competency_questions.question: What does a complete deployment engagement cover, who decides what during it, and what exactly counts as done?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEPLOYMENT_SCOPE_FRAME states the charter, workstreams, named decision-makers and written success criteria, and DEPLOYMENT_HANDOFF_GATE states the definition-of-done that moves the account to recurring support

competency_questions.question: How do I find every line, number and service the business actually has - including the ones the owner forgot - before I design or port anything?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_DISCOVERY_AUDIT describes the walk-through and bill collection and NUMBER_INVENTORY_AUDIT describes building the frozen, countersigned number list from bills, the CSR, dialing tests and public listings

competency_questions.question: What non-voice devices ride the existing copper or account, and how do I keep the port from silently killing the alarm, the fax or the card terminal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANALOG_DEPENDENCY_SURVEY enumerates the device classes, the disposition options for each, and the rule that life-safety lines are referred to the responsible vendor before any disconnect order exists

competency_questions.question: How do I map this customer's people and places to seat types and features without over-provisioning the bill or under-provisioning day one, and what does the pattern for their vertical prescribe?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEAT_FEATURE_MAPPING gives the per-role seat and feature mapping with its pricing honesty rule and VERTICAL_DEPLOYMENT_PATTERNS gives the dental/restaurant/motel/trucking/office starting templates and the rule that the site map overrides the template

competency_questions.question: When do I sell new desk phones, when do I deploy softphones, and when do I reuse the customer's existing devices?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENDPOINT_STRATEGY states the per-seat decision factors (margin, mobility, quality control, provisioning risk, E911 implications) and the bench-test rule before reuse is promised

competency_questions.question: How do I design an auto-attendant, ring groups and schedules that the business will actually use, with no call path that dead-ends?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CALL_FLOW_DESIGN requires every inbound number to have an explicit destination, every path to terminate at an owned endpoint, and a walk-through review with the customer decision-maker dialing the flows

competency_questions.question: What makes a port order reject, how do I prepare one that passes the first time, and what is the recovery loop when it rejects anyway?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORT_ORDER_PREPARATION lists the CSR-reconciliation elements (authorized name, exact service address, account number, PIN, freezes, pending orders) and PORT_REJECTION_RECOVERY gives the read-fix-resubmit-rebaseline loop with escalation mechanisms

competency_questions.question: How do I sequence port activation so the business never loses inbound calls during the transition and never loses the number itself?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PORT_ACTIVATION_SEQUENCE states the build-before-FOC rule, the bridging tactics across the flip, per-number inbound verification, and the never-cancel-the-losing-service-before-confirmation rule with its rationale

competency_questions.question: How do I decide whether this site's internet and LAN can carry the seat count's calls, and what do I change when they cannot?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NETWORK_READINESS_ASSESSMENT gives the busy-hour measurement and concurrent-call demand mechanism with a pass / pass-with-changes / fail verdict, and QOS_LAN_CONFIGURATION gives the VLAN, DSCP, SIP-ALG, PoE and edge-device remediation set

competency_questions.question: What happens to this customer's phones when the internet or power fails, and what am I allowed to promise about it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAILOVER_CONTINUITY_DESIGN describes the forward-on-unreachable, backup-WAN, UPS and carrier-level survival layers with the pull-the-plug demonstration, and HONEST_EXPECTATION_SETTING binds every continuity claim to tested behavior or published platform commitments

competency_questions.question: What E911 and regulatory obligations does this deployment raise, and how do I configure, verify and document them instead of guessing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: E911_CONFIGURATION covers per-device dispatchable locations, the Kari's Law and RAY BAUM obligation classes with the verify-current-rules requirement, softphone location behavior and sanctioned verification, and REGULATORY_FLAG_REGISTER routes USF-class, consent-law-class and privacy-class flags to qualified verification with an auditable record

competency_questions.question: How do I plan cutover day, train the staff beforehand, prove the system works, and stabilize it before handing the account to support?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CUTOVER_RUNBOOK gives the scripted sequence with rollback trigger, STAFF_TRAINING_PROGRAM gives role-based pre-cutover training, ACCEPTANCE_TEST_MATRIX gives the countersigned test rows, and HYPERCARE_STABILIZATION gives the post-cutover ownership window and tuning pass

glossary.definition: The losing carrier's record of the customer's account: the authorized name, exact service address, account number, and the numbers and features on the account. Port orders are reconciled against the CSR line-by-line because any mismatch between the order and the CSR is a rejection waiting to happen.

The document, signed by a person authorized on the losing account, that permits the winning carrier to move the customer's numbers. The signer's name and the service address on the LOA must match the CSR, not the customer's letterhead.

The date the losing carrier commits to release the numbers after accepting a port order. Nothing before FOC is a real date; cutover scheduling, customer promises and old-service cancellation all key off FOC, never off hope.

The losing carrier's refusal of a port order, always for a stated reason code - name mismatch, address mismatch, wrong account number, missing PIN, a freeze on the account, or a pending order. Each rejection costs a resubmission cycle and moves every dependent date.

Porting some but not all numbers on an account. Dangerous in two directions: it can strand hunt-group members on the old carrier so inbound callers hit busy signals, and it can trigger the losing carrier to re-rate or disconnect the services left behind.

A device that presents an analog port to legacy equipment - fax machines, cordless phones, door phones - and carries the call over the VoIP service. Workable for fax with tuned settings and realistic expectations; never acceptable for alarm panels or other life-safety dialers.

The location data an emergency call must convey so responders can find the caller: street address plus the floor, suite, or room detail appropriate to the premises. Every device that can dial out needs one registered, and it must move when the device moves.

A router feature that rewrites SIP packets in transit, intended to help VoIP through NAT and notorious for breaking registrations, one-way audio and dropped transfers. Checking and usually disabling it on the customer's router is among the most common field fixes in the trade.

A set of lines arranged so a call to the main number that finds it busy rolls to the next line. Legacy hunt arrangements hide numbers the owner never dials and must be captured whole in the inventory, because porting only the lead number strands the rest.

The deliberately over-resourced support window immediately after cutover - direct access to the deploying technician, daily punch-list sweeps, and live call-quality monitoring - that ends with a formal review rather than by quietly fading out.
