nodes.definition: Fix what the deployment engagement covers before any hardware is ordered: the project runs from countersigned order to a stabilized system formally handed to recurring support, and its success criteria are written down - every business number ported and confirmed, every seat registered and passing calls, E911 verified, staff trained, customer signed off. The charter names the three workstreams that run in parallel from day one (number porting, site build, network readiness), the owner of each, and the customer-side decision-maker empowered to answer questions about hours, ring order and greetings, because a deployment with no named decision-maker stalls at every small choice. It also states what deployment does not include: the channel-economics questions settled at sale time, and the ongoing support relationship that begins only after the handoff gate.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the engagement scope, the workstream split, or the support-handoff contract is restated

pros.claim: A written definition-of-done stops the project from bleeding into unpaid perpetual tinkering
pros.example: a motel deployment closes against its charter checklist instead of drifting into months of free tweak visits

cons.claim: A rigid charter can turn genuine mid-project discoveries into adversarial change-order fights
cons.example: billing a dentist a change order for an operatory the walk-through missed sours the account before the first invoice

failure_modes: no customer decision-maker named, so hours and ring-order questions stall for weeks
success criteria left implicit, making 'done' a negotiation at the worst moment
the porting workstream started late because it was treated as sequential rather than parallel
acceptance_tests: the charter states port-complete, seats-live, E911-verified, training-done and sign-off as explicit success criteria, names an owner per workstream, and names the customer decision-maker
revisit_triggers: the sold scope and what discovery finds on site diverge materially
the handoff contract with the recurring-support side changes

nodes.definition: Set the customer's expectations to what the deployment can verifiably deliver, in writing, before cutover pressure begins. Porting timelines are controlled by the losing carrier and are quoted as ranges that firm up only at FOC; VoIP behaves differently from copper when power or internet fails, so the specific failover behavior configured for this site is demonstrated rather than promised in the abstract; savings claims are computed only against the customer's actual collected bills; uptime language is limited to the platform's own published commitments plus the site's tested failover design. This node exists because deployment is where sales promises meet physics: the reseller who corrects an overpromise before cutover keeps the account, while the one who lets it surface as a day-one surprise manufactures the churn the recurring-service side must then fight.

included: uptime language bounded by verified basis
excluded: SLA drafting for the ongoing contract

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a promised element loses its verified basis or a new claim is requested of the deployment team

pros.claim: Disclosure-first framing converts outage behavior from a post-incident betrayal into a designed, accepted tradeoff
pros.example: a trucking dispatcher who watched the LTE-failover demo treats a later fiber cut as a known mode, not a broken promise

cons.claim: Candor about porting uncertainty and outage behavior can lose deals to rivals who promise hard dates and zero downtime
cons.example: a motel signs with a competitor guaranteeing a Friday cutover, then suffers exactly the slip you declined to hide

failure_modes: promising a port date before the FOC exists
an uptime or savings figure stated with no verified basis behind it
outage behavior buried in contract fine print instead of demonstrated
acceptance_tests: every timeline, savings and continuity statement made to the customer traces to a verifiable source: an FOC, the collected bills, a tested failover run, or the platform's published commitment
revisit_triggers: the FOC moves or the failover design changes after expectations were set
a sales-side claim is discovered that deployment cannot support

nodes.definition: Walk the site and inventory current telephony reality before designing anything: every handset and where it sits, how inbound calls actually flow (who answers, who covers lunch, where overflow lands), business hours and the after-hours arrangement, the wiring closet, switch and router make and model, cable runs and drop counts, the internet service, and the current carrier bills collected for every location and account. The bill review is the core move - it exposes lines, features and recurring charges the owner forgot exist, and it is the only honest basis for any savings comparison later. The output is a site survey document that the seat map, the number inventory, the analog survey and the network assessment all build on, so an error here propagates into all four.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: site facts change or a downstream node finds the survey contradicted on site

pros.claim: One structured walk catches what remote quoting always misses
pros.example: the restaurant's 'four lines' turn out to be three voice lines plus a credit-card terminal line the remote quote would have destroyed

cons.claim: Deep discovery costs unbilled hours that small deals cannot absorb
cons.example: a two-seat insurance office warrants the bill pull and a photo checklist, not a half-day audit

failure_modes: designing from the sales quote instead of the walk
bills never collected, so hidden lines surface for the first time at port submission
nobody interviewed about lunch coverage and after-hours reality, so the call-flow design fights the staff's actual habits
acceptance_tests: the survey document contains the handset map, the answering-behavior notes, photos of the closet and edge gear, and a complete set of current bills
revisit_triggers: a second suite, location or account is discovered mid-project
the customer changes premises or staffing before cutover

nodes.definition: Enumerate every non-voice device riding the existing copper lines or the current phone account before any port or disconnect order is written: fax machines, fire and burglar alarm panel dialers, elevator phones, gate and door buzzers, credit-card terminals, postage meters, and DSL internet delivered over a voice line. Each device gets an explicit disposition - keep a copper line for it, move it to an ATA with the known reliability caveats stated, migrate it to a purpose-built path (a cellular alarm communicator installed by the alarm company, an e-fax service), or confirm it is genuinely dead. Alarm and elevator lines are life-safety adjacent: the reseller flags and refers them to the responsible licensed vendor and never treats their migration as a do-it-yourself item, and no disconnect order exists until every disposition is recorded.

included: device-class enumeration on every copper pair and account line
excluded: performing alarm or elevator line migration
fax workflow redesign beyond the transport choice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a device inventory miss is found on any deployment, or a disposition option (e.g. an e-fax path) changes viability

pros.claim: The survey prevents the classic disaster where the port completes and the alarm goes silent
pros.example: a motel's fire-alarm dialer found on line two triggers an alarm-company referral weeks before cutover instead of a dead panel discovered after

cons.claim: Dispositions add vendors and cost the customer resents paying alongside the phone project
cons.example: a dentist balks at the alarm company's cellular-communicator charge appearing on top of the phone quote

failure_modes: canceling the copper account with DSL internet riding on it, taking the business dark twice at once
assuming a fax line is idle because nobody at the front desk remembers it
putting an alarm dialer behind an ATA because it seemed to work in a quick test
acceptance_tests: every copper pair and account line has a listed device or an explicit 'nothing rides this line' finding, every device has a disposition, and each life-safety device has a named referred vendor before any disconnect order is drafted
revisit_triggers: a new device is discovered after the survey closed
the losing carrier's disconnect scope turns out broader than the port order intended

nodes.definition: Build the authoritative list of every telephone number the business owns or advertises, because the number that gets forgotten is the one the port kills: main lines, hunt-group and rollover members, direct lines, fax numbers, toll-free numbers, tracking numbers pointed at the business by marketing vendors, and the numbers printed on the door, the trucks, the website and the online listings. Sources are the collected bills, a CSR pulled from the losing carrier, live dialing tests, and a sweep of public-facing listings. Each number is classified port, leave, or release, tracking numbers are identified as vendor-owned and routed through the vendor's own process, and the finished inventory is frozen and countersigned before the LOA is drafted - a number found late forces a supplemental port order and a second cutover event.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a late number discovery on any project, or a change in how the losing carrier releases CSR data

pros.claim: The CSR pull surfaces numbers the owner does not know he pays for
pros.example: a trucking company's CSR reveals two hunt members and a forgotten fax number billed for years, all of which would have stranded on a lead-number-only port

cons.claim: Chasing every advertised number can burn cycles on numbers that are not the customer's to port
cons.example: a restaurant's ad-campaign tracking number belongs to the marketing vendor and follows that vendor's process, not the port order

failure_modes: porting the lead number only and stranding the hunt group
a toll-free number missed because it never appears on the local carrier's bill
the inventory kept informally so nobody can say later which list the LOA was built from
acceptance_tests: every number carries a source citation (bill, CSR, dialing test, or listing sweep) and a port/leave/release class, and the customer countersigned the frozen inventory before the LOA was drafted
revisit_triggers: any number surfaces after the freeze
the CSR and the bills disagree on what the account contains

nodes.definition: Translate discovery into a per-person, per-place seat map: each user or common area gets a seat type (full user, common-area phone, conference room, paging endpoint) and a feature set that reflects the actual job - who needs voicemail-to-email, who sits in which ring group, who may use call recording (flagged against the consent-law class before it is enabled), who needs park, paging or intercom. Because service is priced per seat, the map is also the honest quantity basis of the monthly bill: over-provisioning pads MRR today and invites the resentful downgrade conversation later, while under-provisioning creates day-one coverage gaps that read as a botched install. The map is reviewed with the decision-maker role-by-role, not emailed as a spreadsheet.

included: seat-type assignment per person and place

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a role, headcount or layout change, or a feature's regulatory flag disposition changes

pros.claim: Right-sized seats make the monthly bill defensible line by line at every future renewal
pros.example: hygiene bays get common-area phones instead of five full user seats, and the dentist can see why every line item exists

cons.claim: Per-role precision costs owner interview time that busy customers resist giving
cons.example: a restaurant owner who will not sit for the role review gets a guessed map that misroutes the host stand on opening night

failure_modes: copying seat counts from the sales quote instead of the walk
granting every feature to everyone and drowning the training session
enabling call recording before the consent-law class for the jurisdictions involved was flagged
acceptance_tests: every person and common area appears exactly once with a seat type and feature set, and any recording feature carries a consent-law-class flag disposition
revisit_triggers: staffing or layout changes before cutover
the vertical template and the observed site disagree on a role

nodes.definition: Maintain deployment templates for the verticals this business targets, because the same pattern repeats within a niche and encoding it saves discovery time on every deal. Dental offices need front-desk-heavy flows, an after-hours emergency path to the on-call dentist or answering service, and caution with voicemail-to-email and transcription because messages can contain patient information - flag the healthcare-privacy class rather than self-advising. Restaurants need loud-environment ring behavior, a host-stand phone that parks a caller in two touches, and hours menus that track the kitchen, not the lobby sign. Motels need room phones, front-desk console behavior, wake-up call handling, and explicit review of direct-911-and-notification behavior for guest rooms. Trucking dispatch needs high simultaneous-call capacity, softphones for drivers, and hunt behavior that never rings dead air. Small offices are the generic base. Every template is a starting draft that the per-site map overrides on any observed difference.

included: per-vertical starting seat and flow patterns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repeated per-site overrides or a change in a vertical's operating pattern

pros.claim: A niche template turns the second dental office into a half-day design instead of a from-scratch exercise
pros.example: the after-hours emergency path and hygiene-bay seat pattern from the last practice apply nearly verbatim to the next one

cons.claim: Templates invite skipping the site walk and shipping a pattern the site contradicts
cons.example: the motel template assumes a staffed front desk at night, but this property runs unattended after ten and needs a different emergency-notification design

failure_modes: template applied without the site walk that would contradict it
a vertical compliance flag (guest-room 911 behavior, patient-information voicemail) dropped because the template was trusted as complete
templates never updated, so the same override is rediscovered on every deal
acceptance_tests: the chosen template is named in the design record along with every site-specific override applied to it
revisit_triggers: the same override repeats across deployments in a vertical
a vertical's regulatory flag set changes

nodes.definition: Decide device by device between new desk phones, softphones, and reuse of what the customer already owns. New hardware earns installation margin, arrives pre-provisioned and standardizes support, but inflates the up-front quote the customer compares against rivals. Softphones cost little and suit mobile roles - drivers, the on-call dentist, the owner who works from home - but tie call quality to the user's own device and headset, and complicate E911 because the location moves. Reusing the customer's existing SIP phones preserves their sunk cost and can win the deal, but carries locked-firmware, ownership-transfer and provisioning risk that is bench-tested per model before it is ever promised; analog devices are reused only through an ATA with its caveats stated. The decision is made per seat against the map, never as one global answer for the site.

included: softphone suitability and its E911 implication

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a bench-test outcome, a platform provisioning change, or a readiness finding that alters device assumptions

pros.claim: A tested reuse offer can win a deal a rip-and-replace quote loses
pros.example: bench-testing the dental office's recent SIP phone fleet and reusing it undercuts the competitor who quoted all-new hardware

cons.claim: Reused devices can consume more labor than their value
cons.example: an old carrier-locked phone model eats hours of provisioning attempts that exceed the price of a new handset

failure_modes: promising reuse before the bench test
softphone-only seats granted to roles that call 911 from changing locations with no location-update behavior configured
the ATA treated as a universal answer for every analog device including ones it must never carry
acceptance_tests: every seat in the map has a device decision with its rationale, every reuse promise cites a completed bench test, and every softphone seat carries its E911 location-behavior note
revisit_triggers: a bench test fails after the quote assumed reuse
the network readiness verdict removes PoE or Wi-Fi assumptions the device plan relied on

nodes.definition: Design how calls actually move: auto-attendant menus kept short and phrased in the business's own language, business-hours and holiday schedules, ring groups and hunt order, no-answer and overflow paths, voicemail boxes and their delivery, on-hold audio, and the after-hours path. Two completeness rules govern the work: every inbound number in the inventory gets an explicit destination, and every path terminates at a human, a voicemail box someone owns, or an announced closure - nothing rings forever and nothing dead-ends silently. The finished design is reviewed with the customer decision-maker by dialing the flows aloud together, because owners will approve a diagram they do not understand and then hate the behavior it produces on day one.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: live-traffic evidence from hypercare or a change to hours, staffing or numbers

pros.claim: The every-path-terminates rule eliminates the silent dead-ends that bleed callers
pros.example: walking the tree finds the holiday schedule routing to an unassigned voicemail box before a caller ever does

cons.claim: Design depth beyond what the business can operate becomes shelfware
cons.example: a five-branch attendant tree for a six-person office gets bypassed by staff who just want the phone to ring at the desk

failure_modes: an inbound number left with no explicit destination and discovered by a customer's missed call
menus written in provider jargon instead of the business's own words
the design approved from a diagram without ever dialing it
acceptance_tests: a destination table covers one hundred percent of the number inventory, a path walk shows every branch terminating at an owned endpoint, and the dial-through review with the decision-maker is recorded as done
revisit_triggers: hypercare traffic shows a flow being bypassed or misrouting
hours, staffing or the after-hours arrangement change

nodes.definition: Prepare each port order so the losing carrier has no ground to reject it: the LOA signed by a person authorized on the losing account whose name matches the CSR, the service address written exactly as the CSR shows it down to suite spelling, the account number and any port-out PIN or passcode obtained from the losing carrier, freezes lifted, no pending orders open on the account, and the number list matched to the CSR line by line with partial-port consequences (stranded hunt members, re-rated leftover services) explicitly dispositioned. Rejections are mechanical, not mysterious - name mismatch, address mismatch, wrong account number, missing PIN, freeze, pending order - and every one of them is preventable by reconciling the order against a fresh CSR before submission, while every one that ships costs a rejection cycle measured in days against the cutover date.

excluded: rejection recovery once an order has bounced

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rejection pattern from a specific losing carrier, or an industry change to port-out authentication

pros.claim: CSR-first preparation converts porting from a lottery into a checklist
pros.example: catching that the losing account still carries the practice's previous owner as authorized name, and fixing authorization before submission instead of eating two rejection cycles

cons.claim: CSR retrieval itself can add days of lead time the schedule must absorb
cons.example: a losing carrier that only releases the CSR to the account holder by mail pushes the whole porting workstream out before anything else can move

failure_modes: the LOA signed by an owner whose name is not on the losing account
the service address transcribed from letterhead instead of the CSR
a partial port submitted without dispositioning what remains on the old account
acceptance_tests: the submitted order matches a CSR pulled for this submission on authorized name, service address, account number and number list, PIN present where required, freezes and pending orders cleared, and each number's partial-port consequence dispositioned
revisit_triggers: the CSR is stale relative to recent account changes
the losing carrier changes its port-out authentication requirements

nodes.definition: When a port order rejects anyway, run the recovery loop instead of flailing: read the rejection reason code, fix exactly the mismatched element against a freshly pulled CSR, resubmit, and rebaseline the FOC and every date that hangs off it - telling the customer immediately with the new range rather than letting the cutover date silently slip into fiction. Escalation mechanisms exist in layers: the winning carrier's porting desk first, supervisory escalation for repeated or apparently bogus rejections, and for genuinely stuck ports the losing carrier's executive-relations and regulator-complaint channels, described as mechanisms whose leverage is documentation - the order history and reason codes are the evidence. Rejection causes are tracked per losing carrier, because patterns (one always demands the PIN, another rejects on suite formatting) become permanent checklist lines in preparation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new rejection reason pattern or a change in a carrier's escalation behavior

pros.claim: A disciplined loop keeps a rejection from cascading into a credibility collapse
pros.example: same-day correction and resubmission with a proactive customer call preserves trust even as the FOC moves a week

cons.claim: Escalation spent early burns leverage needed for genuinely stuck ports
cons.example: raising a supervisor fight over a routine name-mismatch fix leaves no headroom when a real months-long stuck port needs the pressure

failure_modes: resubmitting the same order unchanged and collecting the same rejection
the customer learning of the slip from the dead cutover date instead of from you
no rejection log, so the same carrier quirk bites every future deal
acceptance_tests: each rejection records its reason code, the exact corrected element, the resubmission, and the rebaselined dates communicated to the customer
revisit_triggers: the same reason code recurs for one losing carrier
a port exceeds the expected range and needs the next escalation layer

nodes.definition: Sequence activation so the business never loses inbound calls during the transition and never loses the number itself. The new system is built, registered and tested before the FOC date; on FOC day the number flips at the carrier level, so bridging tactics - temporary forwarding or simultaneous-ring where the losing carrier supports them - cover the propagation window; inbound is verified on every ported number the moment the port completes, from an outside line, one by one. The iron rule: the customer never cancels the losing service until every number is confirmed live on the new carrier, because a number on a canceled account can be disconnected rather than ported and a disconnected number can be lost to the business entirely - the single most catastrophic error in this trade. Old service is then canceled deliberately, in writing, with the analog-dependency lines explicitly excluded from the disconnect order.

excluded: the wider cutover-day runbook this sequence slots into

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier changes its bridging options or its treatment of numbers on canceled accounts

pros.claim: The never-cancel-first rule makes the worst outcome in the trade structurally impossible
pros.example: a motel owner eager to stop paying the old bill is held off two weeks, and when the port stalls the numbers are still safe on the living account

cons.claim: Holding both services open means a period of double-paying the customer resents
cons.example: the dentist pays the old carrier and the new per-seat service for the overlap month and wants the difference explained on the invoice

failure_modes: old service canceled before port confirmation and a number lost outright
no bridging configured, so inbound goes dark during propagation on the business's busiest line
port declared complete without dialing every number from outside
acceptance_tests: the activation record shows pre-FOC test completion, the bridging tactic used, an inbound verification entry per ported number, and a written cancellation issued only after all confirmations with analog lines excluded
revisit_triggers: the FOC moves after bridging was scheduled
a number fails inbound verification post-flip

nodes.definition: Establish whether the site's network can carry the seat count's concurrent calls before quality is ever promised. Measure the internet link's upload and download capacity, latency, jitter and packet loss at the site's busy hour - a quiet-morning speed test says nothing about the dinner rush - and set concurrent-call demand from the seat map against the per-call bandwidth requirement the chosen platform publishes, upload being the side that usually binds. Survey the LAN: PoE budget against the phone count, switch capability for VLANs and QoS, cable plant condition, consumer-grade gear daisy-chained into closets, and the contending traffic that shares the link (guest Wi-Fi, cloud backups, ordering tablets, cameras). The output is a written pass, pass-with-changes, or fail verdict with the change list priced - never a silent hope that it will probably be fine.

included: concurrent-call demand versus platform-published per-call requirement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measurement contradicted by live experience, or a platform change to its published per-call requirements

pros.claim: A written verdict before promises protects both margin and reputation
pros.example: the restaurant's saturated upload at dinner service is caught in assessment and priced as an ISP upgrade, not discovered as garbled calls on opening weekend

cons.claim: A conservative verdict can add cost that kills a marginal deal
cons.example: requiring a switch replacement at a four-seat office where best-effort would likely have coped prices the project past the competitor

failure_modes: testing off-peak and certifying a link that collapses at the busy hour
counting download while the upload side binds
PoE budget never checked, discovered when half the phones will not power on install day
acceptance_tests: the readiness report contains busy-hour measurements, the concurrent-call demand calculation citing the platform's published per-call requirement, the LAN and PoE findings, and a signed pass / pass-with-changes / fail verdict
revisit_triggers: seat count or contending traffic changes after the verdict
hypercare quality metrics contradict the assessment baseline

nodes.definition: Configure the network so voice survives contention rather than merely working on a quiet day: a voice VLAN or equivalent separation from data traffic, DSCP marking honored end-to-end across the LAN and prioritized upstream at the router - upstream saturation, not downstream, is the usual call-killer - SIP ALG located and usually disabled on the customer's router where it mangles registrations and causes one-way audio, PoE delivery confirmed against the phone count with the budget arithmetic written down, and device provisioning locked so a phone reset does not fall off the plan. Where the customer's existing router or ISP-supplied gateway cannot do this work, the design either replaces the edge device as a priced change or records the accepted risk in writing with the customer's signature - it never silently hopes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a quality regression traced to network configuration, or an edge-device change at the site

pros.claim: Configured priority keeps the phones working through the traffic the business generates itself
pros.example: the office's cloud backup kicking off at four no longer flattens the receptionist's calls once voice is prioritized upstream

cons.claim: Deep QoS work on customer-owned gear creates a maintenance surface the reseller now implicitly owns
cons.example: the customer's IT volunteer resets the router months later, wiping the voice priority rules, and the resulting call complaints land on the reseller

failure_modes: SIP ALG left enabled and misdiagnosed for weeks as a platform problem
DSCP markings stripped at an unmanaged switch nobody surveyed
QoS configured downstream only while the upload side stays saturated
acceptance_tests: the as-built network record shows the separation scheme, the marking and shaping configuration, the SIP ALG disposition, the PoE arithmetic, and either the replaced edge device or the signed accepted-risk note
revisit_triggers: hypercare quality metrics degrade against the baseline
the customer changes router, ISP or switch hardware

nodes.definition: Design what happens when things fail, and demonstrate it rather than describe it. The layers: carrier-level rules that survive total site loss (unreachable-device routing to voicemail, a mobile app, a cell number or an answering service, configured at the platform so they work when the building is dark), automatic forward-to-cell for the numbers that must always answer, an LTE or secondary-WAN backup path where the seat count and the cost of missed calls justify it, and UPS coverage sized for the switch, router and the phones that must ride out short outages. Behavior is proven by pulling the plug in front of the customer and watching where calls land, and what is promised afterward is exactly what the test showed - the no-guaranteed-uptime boundary lives here, because continuity is a designed set of behaviors with limits, not an assurance.

excluded: SLA credit structures of the ongoing contract

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an outage event, a platform change to unreachable-routing behavior, or a change in the customer's continuity needs

pros.claim: A demonstrated failover turns the scariest VoIP objection into a selling point
pros.example: the dispatcher watches the internet drop and driver calls roll to the on-call cell within the same minute, and the objection dissolves

cons.claim: Full continuity layering can be over-engineering for the customer's actual risk
cons.example: an LTE backup and rack UPS quoted for a two-seat office whose calls could simply forward to the owner's cell during rare outages

failure_modes: failover configured but never tested, failing during the first real outage
carrier-level rules absent so a dead site takes calls to nowhere instead of voicemail
the UPS covering the phones but not the switch that powers them
acceptance_tests: the continuity design lists each failure mode with its configured behavior, and a witnessed pull-the-plug test record shows where calls actually landed
revisit_triggers: a real outage exposes behavior differing from the test
the customer's risk profile changes (new hours, new dependence on inbound calls)

nodes.definition: Treat emergency calling as a hard gate on every deployment, never a checkbox. Every device that can place a call gets a registered dispatchable location - street address plus the floor, suite or room detail responders need to find the caller - and multi-line systems are configured for the Kari's Law class of obligations (direct 911 dialing with no prefix, on-site notification when 911 is dialed) and the RAY BAUM class (dispatchable location conveyed with the call), with the reseller verifying the current requirements for this jurisdiction and platform at deployment time rather than trusting memory of the rules. Softphone and other nomadic users get location-update behavior configured and explained to them, because their registered address is wrong the moment they leave it. Motels get room-level location detail and a front-desk notification review. Verification uses the carrier's sanctioned address-verification test procedure - never casual live 911 calls outside the documented, PSAP-respecting process.

included: direct-dial and notification behavior of the Kari's Law class
location conveyance of the RAY BAUM class
excluded: legal advice on the statutes themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in emergency-calling rules, platform E911 behavior, or any device location at the site

pros.claim: Gating go-live on verified E911 protects lives and removes the deployment's worst liability exposure in one move
pros.example: the walk finds a softphone seat registered to the office while its user works from home, and the fix ships before cutover instead of after an emergency

cons.claim: Per-device location work on multi-room premises is slow and easy to resent under schedule pressure
cons.example: registering room-level detail across a forty-room motel adds a day nobody budgeted, and the pressure to skip it is real

failure_modes: a device left on the platform's default or the reseller's own address
direct-dial or notification behavior assumed from memory of the rules instead of verified for the current jurisdiction and platform
softphones deployed with no location-update behavior configured or explained
verification skipped because the schedule slipped
acceptance_tests: every dial-capable device shows a registered dispatchable location, direct-dial and notification behavior is verified against current requirements for the jurisdiction and platform, nomadic seats show configured location-update behavior, and a sanctioned verification record exists per site
revisit_triggers: any device moves, is added, or changes user
the jurisdiction's or platform's emergency-calling requirements change

nodes.definition: Keep a live register of the regulatory and tax flags each deployment raises and route every one to qualified verification instead of in-house guessing. USF-class contribution and telecom-tax treatment differs with the channel model - an agent, a reseller of record and a white-label operator carry different obligations - so the firm's actual duties are confirmed by a telecom-tax professional or the platform's compliance resources, never assumed from a forum post. Call-recording features are enabled only after the consent-law class for every jurisdiction the customer calls into is flagged and dispositioned. Healthcare-adjacent customers such as dental practices get privacy-class flags on voicemail-to-email, transcription and recording features. Alarm-line changes are referred to licensed alarm vendors. The register records each flag, its disposition, who verified it and when - it turns 'verify current rules' from a vibe into an auditable artifact the handoff gate can check.

included: flag classes: USF/telecom-tax, consent-law, healthcare-privacy, life-safety referral
excluded: rendering the legal or tax opinions themselves
channel model selection that drives the tax treatment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the firm's channel model, an amendment in a flagged rule class, or a new regulated feature request

pros.claim: A written register makes compliance survivable by ordinary people under deadline pressure
pros.example: the recording feature for the trucking dispatcher stays disabled until the register shows the consent-class flag dispositioned, no matter who is in a hurry

cons.claim: Professional verification costs money and days on deals that feel routine
cons.example: holding a small office's recording feature for counsel review reads as bureaucracy to a customer who just wants the button on

failure_modes: tax treatment assumed to match a different channel model than the one actually operated
recording enabled with the consent flag never dispositioned
flags tracked in someone's head and lost at handoff
acceptance_tests: the register lists every flag raised by this deployment with class, disposition, verifier and date, and the handoff gate can read it without asking anyone
revisit_triggers: the channel model changes
a rule class the register cites is amended
a new feature with regulatory surface is enabled post-deployment

nodes.definition: Script cutover day before it happens rather than improvising it live. The date is chosen against the FOC and the vertical's low-traffic window - never a restaurant on Friday night, never trucking dispatch on Monday at six - and the runbook lays out a timed sequence: confirm port completion, verify inbound per number, walk the call flows, check fax and ATA devices, confirm E911 registrations, with named roles for who executes and who watches, and the customer decision-maker reachable on site. The rollback plan is written next to the sequence, not invented under stress: temporary forwarding back to the losing carrier while that account still lives, the spare analog path if one was kept, and an explicit, pre-agreed trigger condition for invoking rollback. A cutover without a written rollback trigger becomes a hostage negotiation with itself when something breaks at four in the afternoon.

included: date selection against FOC and traffic window

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a date slip, a failed rehearsal assumption, or a change in the rollback path's availability

pros.claim: A pre-agreed rollback trigger converts a mid-cutover failure from a panic into a procedure
pros.example: when inbound verification fails on two numbers at the agreed trigger point, forwarding snaps back to the old carrier and the restaurant takes dinner reservations while the fix runs

cons.claim: Heavy scripting can over-fit the plan and slow adaptation when reality diverges
cons.example: the runbook assumes the port completes by noon; when it lands at three, a team glued to the script burns the window instead of re-sequencing

failure_modes: cutover scheduled into the vertical's peak window
no rollback plan, so a failure strands the business with no working phones in either system
roles unassigned, so three people fix one problem while nobody watches inbound
acceptance_tests: the runbook shows the FOC-anchored date rationale, the timed sequence with named roles, the rollback method and its explicit trigger condition, and the decision-maker's confirmed availability
revisit_triggers: the FOC or a gating workstream slips
a rehearsal or rejection event changes the sequence assumptions

nodes.definition: Prove the system works with a written matrix executed and countersigned, not with a shrug that the phones seem fine. Rows: inbound to every number in the inventory from an outside line, outbound with correct caller-ID name and number per seat, every attendant branch and schedule including the holiday entries, ring groups and overflow behavior, voicemail deposit and delivery for every box, fax send and receive through each ATA, E911 verification per the carrier's sanctioned procedure, the failover demonstration, and the vertical-specific checks - the motel wake-up call, the dental after-hours emergency path, the dispatcher's simultaneous-call load. Each row records expected behavior and observed result; a failed row either blocks handoff or is accepted in writing as a punch-list item with an owner and a date. The countersigned matrix is the deployment's proof-of-work and the support desk's baseline.

included: flow, voicemail, fax, E911 and failover rows
excluded: load or penetration testing beyond deployment scope

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a defect escaping the matrix into hypercare, or a new row class needed by a vertical

pros.claim: A countersigned matrix ends the era of 'it never worked' disputes before it starts
pros.example: when the motel claims weeks later that faxing never worked, the signed row showing a successful send-receive on cutover day reframes the conversation to what changed since

cons.claim: Exhaustive testing costs cutover-day hours when everyone wants to go home
cons.example: dialing all thirty numbers of a motel's inventory inbound one by one at nine at night tests discipline as much as telephony

failure_modes: sampling a few numbers instead of testing all of them, missing the one that did not port
outbound caller-ID never checked, so the business dials out showing the wrong name for weeks
failures accepted verbally with no owner or date, evaporating into the punch list
acceptance_tests: the matrix covers every inventory number inbound, per-seat outbound caller-ID, every flow branch, every voicemail box, every ATA, E911 verification and failover, and carries the customer countersignature with punch-list items owned and dated
revisit_triggers: a punch-list item ages past its date
any post-cutover change invalidates tested rows

nodes.definition: Train by role before cutover day, never during it. Front-desk and reception staff get deep hands-on practice - transfer, hold versus park, ring-group behavior, retrieving from the queue - because they touch every caller the business has; everyone else gets the five moves their job needs plus a one-page quick reference taped where they actually work; owners and managers get the admin portal tour: changing hours, recording a holiday greeting, pulling a call log. Voicemail boxes are personalized during the session itself so no caller ever reaches an unconfigured box. Adoption is the true deliverable: a technically perfect system the staff cannot drive reads as a failed project, generates the day-one ticket flood the support desk inherits, and poisons the renewal conversation years early.

included: hands-on practice on the real system
excluded: ongoing refresher training in the support relationship

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: adoption friction observed in hypercare or turnover in trained roles

pros.claim: Pre-cutover training absorbs the panic that otherwise becomes day-one support tickets
pros.example: the receptionist who practiced park-and-page on Thursday handles Monday's first rush without a single help call

cons.claim: Training scheduled around a busy staff's shifts can delay the cutover it gates
cons.example: a restaurant that cannot assemble its staff outside service hours pushes training out a week and the cutover with it

failure_modes: training compressed into cutover morning while the team fights fires
one generic session for every role, too shallow for the front desk and too long for everyone else
voicemail personalization left as homework nobody does
acceptance_tests: a training record shows each role's session completed before cutover, voicemail boxes personalized in-session, quick references placed, and the owner able to change hours and greetings unaided
revisit_triggers: staff turnover before or shortly after cutover
a call-flow change that invalidates trained behavior

nodes.definition: Own the first weeks after cutover as part of the deployment, not as early support. Hypercare means heightened availability with a direct line to the deploying technician rather than the general queue, a daily punch-list sweep through week one, monitoring of the registration and call-quality indicators the platform exposes - quality scores and jitter and loss trends read against the readiness baseline - and a deliberate tuning pass on ring-group timing, attendant options and overflow behavior informed by live traffic, which always differs from what the design predicted. Hypercare ends at a scheduled review that either extends it with named reasons or hands off formally; it never just fades out. The window exists because the first weeks decide whether the account starts loyal or resentful, and because real callers expose what no test matrix can.

excluded: the steady-state support model and its economics
churn management of the ongoing account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: quality-trend movement, punch-list recurrence, or a change in the handoff contract with support

pros.claim: Live-traffic tuning fixes the designs that were plausible on paper and wrong in practice
pros.example: week-one traffic shows lunch calls overflowing to a voicemail nobody checks, and the overflow moves to the manager's cell before the customer ever complains

cons.claim: An open-ended hypercare window trains the customer to bypass the support process forever
cons.example: a motel owner still texting the installing technician at month four because hypercare never formally ended

failure_modes: hypercare skipped, so week-one friction hits a support desk with no context
quality indicators unmonitored, letting a degrading trend hide until the customer notices
no end review, so the window fades into permanent free escalation
acceptance_tests: the hypercare record shows the availability window honored, daily sweeps in week one, quality trends read against the readiness baseline, tuning changes logged, and the end review held with its outcome recorded
revisit_triggers: quality trends degrade against baseline
punch-list items recur after being closed

nodes.definition: Gate the transition from project to recurring service on a definition-of-done, because what crosses this line becomes the support desk's inheritance. Pass conditions: all port orders complete and confirmed per number; the acceptance matrix countersigned with its punch list resolved or formally accepted; E911 registrations verified and documented; the regulatory flag register clean or professionally dispositioned; as-built documentation delivered - the number inventory with dispositions, the seat map, call-flow diagrams, network configuration including QoS and failover settings, and the device inventory with credentials handled per the firm's security policy; training completion recorded; and a handoff briefing held so the support desk receives context instead of a mystery box. A gate that fails is held open with the missing items named and dated - never waved through because the invoice wants to close.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: support-side feedback on handoff quality or a change in the definition-of-done contract

pros.claim: A documented gate is the difference between a support desk that fixes and one that re-discovers
pros.example: six months later a new technician resolves a routing complaint in minutes from the as-built call-flow diagram instead of reverse-engineering the tree live

cons.claim: A strict gate can hold revenue recognition hostage to paperwork on a system that genuinely works
cons.example: the final invoice waits on a missing wiring diagram while the customer has been happily taking calls for three weeks

failure_modes: the gate waved through under billing pressure with the punch list quietly open
as-built documentation reconstructed months later from memory instead of captured during the build
no handoff briefing, so support meets the account for the first time inside an angry ticket
acceptance_tests: every pass condition has evidence attached (port confirmations, countersigned matrix, E911 records, flag register, as-built set, training record, briefing note), and any failed condition is named with an owner and date while the gate holds
revisit_triggers: the support side reports missing or wrong as-built information
the definition-of-done contract with the recurring-service side changes

edges.why_related: discovery runs inside the charter's scope and feeds the success criteria the charter names
expectations are set against the charter's written success criteria and workstream timelines
the analog survey works from the lines, closet and bills the discovery walk captured
the seat map is built from the roles, places and answering behavior discovery recorded
the collected bills are a primary source the number inventory reconciles against
the readiness assessment measures the link and LAN the discovery walk inventoried
the vertical template is selected and overridden against the observed seat map
device decisions are made per seat in the map, not globally for the site
analog dispositions decide which devices need ATAs, kept copper, or purpose-built replacements
ring groups, boxes and destinations are drawn from the confirmed seat map
the frozen countersigned inventory is the number list the port order carries
recovery corrects the specific prepared elements a rejection names
activation sequencing keys off the FOC the accepted order produces
QoS work implements the change list the readiness verdict priced
each chosen device type - desk phone, softphone, ATA - carries its own dispatchable-location behavior to configure
the runbook wraps the activation sequence in date choice, roles and rollback
the runbook's flow-walk steps execute the approved call-flow design
cutover assumes the network work is complete, or its runbook inherits open risk
the matrix executes against the live system the runbook produced
the matrix's E911 rows verify the registrations the configuration created
training teaches the flows as designed; an untrained flow is a flow that fails
hypercare works the punch list the matrix produced and monitors what it certified
the gate's end-of-hypercare review is the moment the transition decision is made
the gate reads the flag register and holds on any undispositioned flag
continuity language is bounded to what the tested design and published platform commitments support - no guaranteed-uptime claims
E911 work proceeds only against verified-current requirements, not remembered ones; the register records who verified and when
no hard port or cutover date is promised to the customer before the FOC exists
no go-live while any device lacks a verified dispatchable location - the runbook cannot schedule around this gate
every analog disposition is recorded before any port or disconnect order is drafted, so the order's scope cannot orphan a live device
training completes before cutover day; the runbook assumes staff who already know the system
readiness findings - no PoE budget, weak Wi-Fi, saturated upload - directly change which devices are viable per seat
a rejection-driven FOC rebaseline moves the cutover date and everything scheduled against it
live-traffic observations from hypercare drive the tuning pass on attendant options, ring timing and overflow
quality trends read against the readiness baseline send the deployment back into network configuration when they degrade
reusing the customer's devices and edge gear saves quote money but strips the reseller of the network control that call quality depends on
edges.resolution_rule: the readiness verdict wins: reuse is allowed only for seats and gear that pass the assessment, and where the customer insists on failing gear the accepted risk is signed in writing or the deal is declined

edges.why_related: the customer's preferred cutover date and the FOC the losing carrier grants routinely disagree
edges.resolution_rule: the FOC governs; the cutover date moves to it, temporary forwarding bridges any customer-facing gap, and no runbook date is communicated as firm before the FOC exists

edges.why_related: the template's economical defaults and the site's observed reality pull the seat map in different directions
edges.resolution_rule: the per-site map overrides the template on any observed difference; when the same override recurs across deployments, the template itself is amended

edges.why_related: billing close-out pressure pushes to end hypercare while open punch-list items push to extend it
edges.resolution_rule: the gate's pass conditions win: hypercare extends with named items, owners and dates, and the gate is never waved through for invoice convenience

edges.why_related: both are hidden-asset audits of the legacy account - one hunts devices riding the copper, the other hunts numbers riding the bill - and both must freeze before porting paperwork starts

conflict_axes.name: cutover_speed_vs_port_certainty
conflict_axes.description: The customer wants the new system on a date convenient to them; the port completes on the date the losing carrier grants, and pushing cutover ahead of port certainty risks the number itself.
poles: cut over when the customer wants
cut over when the port is certain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the FOC governs every date; bridging tactics absorb the customer-facing wait, and no date is spoken as firm before FOC

conflict_axes.name: hardware_margin_vs_right_sized_endpoints
conflict_axes.description: New phones at every seat maximize install revenue; softphones and tested reuse right-size the quote but shrink the hardware line the deployment margin lives on.
poles: deploy the cheapest device that serves the seat
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide per seat from the map; win the account with honest sizing and let margin come from work actually needed

conflict_axes.name: template_efficiency_vs_site_truth
conflict_axes.description: Vertical templates make the tenth dental office fast and consistent, but every site deviates somewhere, and a trusted template quietly ships its assumptions over observed reality.
poles: design from this site's observed facts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: template as starting draft, site walk as authority; recurring overrides amend the template

conflict_axes.name: network_control_vs_customer_gear_reuse
conflict_axes.description: Quality is easiest to defend on gear the reseller controls; the customer's existing router, switches and wiring are cheaper but carry SIP ALG surprises, PoE gaps and reset-prone configs.
poles: replace the edge and own the path
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: readiness verdict decides per component; failing gear is replaced as a priced change or its risk accepted in writing

conflict_axes.name: continuity_assurance_vs_honest_claims
conflict_axes.description: Customers want to hear the phones will never go down; the truthful offer is designed failover behavior with demonstrated limits, which sells worse than a guarantee.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: demonstrate the failover live and put in writing exactly what the test showed; no uptime language beyond the platform's own published commitments

conflict_axes.name: compliance_rigor_vs_deployment_margin
conflict_axes.description: Per-device dispatchable locations, verified current rules and professionally dispositioned flags cost unbilled hours on every job; skipping them fattens margin until the day it destroys the firm.
poles: full compliance work on every deployment
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: E911 and flag dispositions are non-negotiable gates priced into every job; margin is recovered elsewhere, never here

conflict_axes.name: feature_richness_vs_adoption_capacity
conflict_axes.description: The platform offers more features than any small business can absorb; enabling everything demonstrates value on paper but drowns training and produces a staff that trusts nothing.
poles: enable what the staff can actually drive
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: map features to roles, train the mapped set deeply, and stage later features into the recurring relationship

conflict_axes.name: parallel_run_safety_vs_double_cost
conflict_axes.description: Keeping the losing service alive through porting and stabilization is the only safe sequence, but the customer pays two carriers for the overlap and pressures for early cancellation.
poles: hold the old service until everything is confirmed
cancel early and stop the double bill
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never cancel before per-number confirmation; explain the overlap as the price of the number's safety at expectation-setting time

conflict_axes.name: project_closure_vs_stabilization_completeness
conflict_axes.description: The books want the project closed and invoiced; the account wants hypercare, punch-list closure and complete as-builts, and closing early converts open items into support-desk mysteries.
poles: close only through the handoff gate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the gate's evidence-backed pass conditions decide; failed conditions hold the gate with named items and dates

edge_cases.description: The port completes and the losing carrier disconnects the whole account - including the DSL internet riding a voice line - taking the business's phones and internet down together
edge_cases.trigger: a full-account port or cancellation with a data service riding the voice account
edge_cases.mitigation: the analog survey flags account-riding services before the order is drafted, and the order explicitly scopes what remains; internet delivery is re-homed before any copper disconnect

edge_cases.description: A fire or burglar alarm panel dialer rides a copper line scheduled for disconnect, and monitoring goes silently dead after cutover
edge_cases.trigger: an alarm dialer on the legacy line missed or ATA'd instead of referred
edge_cases.mitigation: life-safety lines get a named referral to the alarm vendor with the migration confirmed complete before the disconnect order exists; the flag register holds the gate until dispositioned

edge_cases.description: The port order rejects repeatedly because the losing account still carries the business's previous owner as the authorized name
edge_cases.trigger: a business sold or restructured without updating the carrier account
edge_cases.mitigation: the CSR pull exposes the stale authorization early; the customer corrects account authority with the losing carrier before the LOA is submitted

edge_cases.description: A partial port moves the main number but strands the hunt-group rollover members, so busy-hour callers get dead air on the old carrier
edge_cases.trigger: porting the lead number without the hunt members the CSR shows
edge_cases.mitigation: the inventory captures hunt membership from the CSR and the port order carries the group whole or dispositions each member explicitly

edge_cases.description: A softphone user dials 911 from home while the seat's registered dispatchable location is the office across town
edge_cases.trigger: nomadic use with no location-update behavior configured or explained
edge_cases.mitigation: every softphone seat gets location-update behavior configured, the user briefed on it, and the arrangement recorded in the E911 verification record

edge_cases.description: A motel's room phones require a dial-out prefix to reach 911, or the front desk never learns a guest dialed it
edge_cases.trigger: multi-line configuration that predates or ignores the direct-dial and notification obligation class
edge_cases.mitigation: the motel template forces a room-phone 911 review: direct dialing verified with no prefix, notification behavior configured and tested per current requirements

edge_cases.description: The restaurant's ordering tablets and guest Wi-Fi saturate the upload at dinner rush and calls turn to garble at the exact hour the business lives on
edge_cases.trigger: readiness measured off-peak while contending traffic peaks with the business
edge_cases.mitigation: measure at the busy hour, price the upstream fix in the verdict, and prioritize voice upstream before cutover rather than after complaints

edge_cases.description: The customer cancels the old carrier the day the new phones arrive, before any port completes, and the numbers head toward disconnection instead of porting
edge_cases.trigger: double-bill resentment plus nobody stating the never-cancel-first rule
edge_cases.mitigation: the rule and its reason are stated at expectation setting and repeated at every date conversation; if cancellation already happened, the losing carrier is engaged immediately while the account can still be restored

edge_cases.description: The dental office's after-hours emergency calls route to a voicemail box nobody personalized or checks, and a weekend emergency goes unanswered
edge_cases.trigger: an after-hours path terminating at an unowned box
edge_cases.mitigation: the path-completeness rule assigns every terminal box an owner, training personalizes it in-session, and the matrix dials the after-hours path explicitly

edge_cases.description: The office fax behind an ATA works in testing but fails intermittently on the insurance claims the practice depends on
edge_cases.trigger: fax-over-VoIP sensitivity to jitter and codec handling
edge_cases.mitigation: set fax expectations honestly at disposition time, tune the ATA per the platform's fax guidance, monitor through hypercare, and offer the e-fax path where reliability matters more than the machine

edge_cases.description: Cutover lands in the vertical's peak window - dispatch on Monday morning - and a minor glitch becomes a business-stopping event
edge_cases.trigger: date chosen for installer convenience instead of the traffic calendar
edge_cases.mitigation: the runbook selects the vertical's low-traffic window and the template records what that window is for each niche

edge_cases.description: Week one after cutover, the untrained front desk misroutes every transfer and the staff revolts against the new system
edge_cases.trigger: training compressed into cutover morning or skipped for schedule
edge_cases.mitigation: training is a sequenced gate before cutover; hypercare's first sweep watches the front desk specifically and retrains on the spot where friction shows

workflow.action: Charter the deployment and set expectations
workflow.description: Write the success criteria, name workstream owners and the customer decision-maker, and set verifiable expectations on dates, outages and savings
workflow.gate: success criteria, owners, decision-maker and the verified-basis rule for every claim are on paper

workflow.action: Walk the site and collect the bills
workflow.description: Inventory handsets, answering behavior, closet, LAN, internet and every carrier bill
workflow.gate: handset map, answering notes, closet photos and a complete bill set exist

workflow.action: Survey analog dependencies and disposition each
workflow.description: Find every non-voice device on the copper and the account; assign keep, ATA, migrate or confirm-dead; refer life-safety lines
workflow.gate: every line has a device or a nothing-rides-here finding; life-safety devices carry named vendor referrals

workflow.action: Build and freeze the number inventory
workflow.description: Reconcile bills, CSR, dialing tests and public listings into a port/leave/release list the customer countersigns
workflow.gate: every number carries a source citation and class; the freeze predates the LOA

workflow.action: Map seats and features against the vertical pattern
workflow.description: Assign seat types and role-based features, applying the vertical template and recording every override
workflow.artifact: seat and feature map with template overrides
workflow.gate: every person and place appears once; recording features carry consent-class flags; overrides are named

workflow.description: Choose new phone, softphone or bench-tested reuse per seat, with ATA caveats and E911 notes attached
workflow.gate: every reuse promise cites a bench test; every softphone seat carries its location-behavior note

workflow.action: Design and dial-review the call flows
workflow.description: Build attendants, schedules, groups and overflow so every number has a destination and every path terminates
workflow.gate: destination table covers the full inventory and the dial-through review with the decision-maker is done

workflow.action: Assess the network and configure QoS and failover
workflow.description: Measure at busy hour, issue the verdict, then implement separation, priority, SIP-ALG and PoE fixes plus the continuity design with its plug-pull test
workflow.artifact: readiness verdict plus as-built network and continuity record
workflow.gate: verdict signed; QoS as-built recorded; failover demonstrated and its observed behavior written down

workflow.action: Prepare and submit the port orders
workflow.description: Reconcile LOA and order against a fresh CSR, clear PINs, freezes and pending orders, disposition partial-port consequences, submit and track to FOC
workflow.artifact: submitted port order with CSR reconciliation record
workflow.gate: order matches the CSR line-by-line and every number's consequence is dispositioned

workflow.action: Configure and verify E911 with flags dispositioned
workflow.description: Register dispatchable locations per device, verify direct-dial and notification behavior against current rules, configure nomadic location updates, run the sanctioned verification, and disposition the regulatory register
workflow.artifact: E911 verification record and updated flag register
workflow.gate: every dial-capable device verified; the register shows verifier and date on every flag

workflow.description: Run role-tiered sessions before cutover, personalize voicemail in-session, place quick references, train the owner on the portal
workflow.gate: every role trained before cutover day and every voicemail box personalized

workflow.action: Execute cutover, prove it, stabilize it, and hand off
workflow.description: Run the runbook on the FOC-anchored date with rollback armed, execute the countersigned acceptance matrix, hold the hypercare window with its tuning pass, and pass the handoff gate on evidence
workflow.artifact: executed runbook, countersigned matrix, hypercare record, as-built documentation set
workflow.gate: every gate pass condition holds with evidence attached, or the gate is held open with named items and dates

priority_rationale: Frame nodes come first because the charter, the disclosure discipline and the discovery walk determine what every later workstream builds on; porting, network and compliance work run as parallel tracks whose sequencing rules (CSR before order, survey before disconnect, verification before go-live) exist to protect the customer's number, lines and legal exposure; and cutover, acceptance, training, hypercare and the handoff gate come last because they compose the built system into a proven, adopted, documented service the recurring-support side can inherit without archaeology.

dominance_rules.rule: E911 verification dominates every schedule and margin pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an emergency call that fails or misdirects is a human catastrophe and an existential liability; no deadline outranks it
dominance_rules.trigger: any pressure to go live with unverified dispatchable locations or unconfirmed notification behavior
dominance_rules.action: hold the cutover until the E911 verification record is complete

dominance_rules.rule: The FOC dominates every preferred date
dominance_rules.rationale: the losing carrier's commitment is the only real date in the project; everything else is scheduling fiction
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer, salesperson or installer proposes a firm date before FOC
dominance_rules.action: communicate ranges until FOC, then anchor the runbook to it

dominance_rules.rationale: a canceled account can turn a port into a disconnection and cost the business its number permanently
dominance_rules.trigger: the customer moves to cancel the losing service before per-number confirmation
dominance_rules.action: stop the cancellation, restate the rule and its reason, and revisit only after every number is confirmed live

dominance_rules.rule: Analog disposition completeness dominates copper cancellation
dominance_rules.rationale: an undispositioned device on a dropped line means a dead alarm, fax or terminal discovered by failure
dominance_rules.trigger: a disconnect order is drafted while any line lacks a disposition
dominance_rules.action: hold the order until the survey shows every line dispositioned and life-safety referrals confirmed

dominance_rules.rule: The verified basis dominates the persuasive claim
dominance_rules.rationale: an uptime or savings promise without a tested or documented basis is a churn seed and a liability, whatever it closes today
dominance_rules.trigger: any customer-facing claim about dates, savings or continuity lacking its source
dominance_rules.action: restate the claim to what the FOC, the bills, the failover test or the platform's published commitments support

dominance_rules.rule: The readiness verdict dominates reuse economics
dominance_rules.rationale: call quality on a failing network becomes the reseller's reputation regardless of whose gear failed
dominance_rules.trigger: quote pressure to reuse edge gear or links the assessment failed
dominance_rules.action: replace as a priced change or take a signed accepted-risk note; silent hope is not an option

dominance_rules.rule: The site map dominates the vertical template
dominance_rules.rationale: templates encode last site's truth; this site's walk encodes this site's
dominance_rules.trigger: the template and observed site facts disagree on a seat, flow or compliance item
dominance_rules.action: apply the observed fact, record the override, and amend the template if the override recurs

dominance_rules.rule: Qualified verification dominates in-house regulatory guessing
dominance_rules.rationale: USF-class, consent-class and privacy-class exposure is firm-level and model-dependent; a confident guess is still a guess
dominance_rules.trigger: a regulatory or tax question answered internally without a professional or platform-compliance source
dominance_rules.action: route the flag to the qualified verifier and record the disposition in the register

dominance_rules.rationale: an unearned handoff converts deployment debts into support-desk mysteries at interest
dominance_rules.trigger: billing or utilization pressure to close a deployment with failed pass conditions
dominance_rules.action: hold the gate open with named items, owners and dates until evidence exists

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pull the CSR and reconcile the order against it before any port submission
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rejection cycles that burn days each and stack up against the cutover date

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the analog dependency survey before drafting any port or disconnect order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: post-cutover discovery of a dead alarm line, drowned fax or darkened DSL that must be resurrected under emergency pressure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Freeze and countersign the number inventory before the LOA is drafted
anti_rework_rules.prevents: late-found numbers forcing supplemental port orders and a second cutover event

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify network readiness at the busy hour before ordering endpoints or promising quality
anti_rework_rules.prevents: phones shipped against absent PoE, and quality complaints that force network rework after go-live

anti_rework_rules.rule: Configure and verify E911 before cutover, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: emergency-call exposure during the gap and a rushed compliance scramble layered on stabilization
day-one chaos, a ticket flood into hypercare, and retraining under fire that costs double

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build call flows from the confirmed seat map, not the sales quote
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wholesale flow rebuilds when actual roles and staffing contradict what was sold

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the losing service alive through the parallel window with cancellation as a deliberate written act
anti_rework_rules.prevents: the unrecoverable loss of a business number - rework that no amount of labor can perform

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture as-built documentation during the build, not retroactively
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reverse-engineering the deployment months later from memory when support hits its first hard ticket

iteration_protocol.action: correct the named element against a fresh CSR, resubmit, rebaseline the FOC and every dependent date, and tell the customer before the dates tell them

iteration_protocol.trigger: a number, line or device surfaces after the inventory freeze
iteration_protocol.action: reopen the affected inventory, disposition the newcomer, and issue a supplemental port order or disposition record with its own dates

iteration_protocol.trigger: call-quality complaints or degrading platform metrics during hypercare
iteration_protocol.action: compare live metrics to the readiness baseline, isolate LAN versus link versus platform, and retune QoS or escalate the link with evidence in hand

iteration_protocol.trigger: emergency-calling rules or platform E911 behavior change, or any device moves
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify dispatchable locations and notification behavior against current requirements and update the verification record

iteration_protocol.trigger: live traffic shows a call flow bypassed, misrouting or overflowing wrong
iteration_protocol.action: run the tuning pass on the affected flows and retrain the roles whose behavior the change touches

iteration_protocol.trigger: the site changes mid-project - staffing, layout, a new suite, changed hours
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the affected slice of the seat map and endpoint plan, and propagate to flows and E911 registrations

iteration_protocol.trigger: a failover test or a real outage shows behavior different from what was designed or promised
iteration_protocol.action: redesign the failing layer, re-test with the customer watching, and re-issue the continuity statement to match observed behavior

iteration_protocol.trigger: the support desk reports as-built gaps or handoff friction on a closed deployment
iteration_protocol.action: repair the documentation set, feed the gap back into the gate's checklist, and review recent gates for the same omission

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
